sources: Zagier, The Dilogarithm Function, Ch. I SS3 and Ch. II 'The Rogers dilogarithm'

gates.claim: Kirillov's cubic x^3+2x^2-x-1 is this lane's x^3-2x^2-x+1 under x -> -x
Kirillov/Watson's alpha, beta, gamma ARE this lane's -w3, w2, 1/w1
Watson's (1937) three relations hold: 1/7, 10/7, 8/7 times L(1)
this lane's (17,5,-1)/7 are the same classical family -- same field Q(zeta_7)^+, same denominator 7, different combinations of the same L-values
Zagier's extension (L(x)=2L(1)-L(1/x) for x>1, -L(x/(x-1)) for x<0) is exactly FiveTwoRogersExtend.extend -- inversion and Landen hold by definition
Zagier's L'(x) = -log(1-x)/(2x) - log(x)/(2(1-x)) is hasDerivAt_rogersL, verbatim -- and he names it as the route to all the functional equations

verdict.headline: THE LEVEL-7 LADDER IS CLASSICAL. Watson (1937). This lane's Lean result is a FORMALIZATION of a known identity family, not a new derivation.
verdict.correspondence: Kirillov's alpha, beta, gamma are exactly -w3, w2, 1/w1, and his cubic is ours under x -> -x. Verified to 1e-30.
verdict.what_is_still_this_lane's: the ROUTE and the FORMALIZATION. Kirillov proves accessibility from the duplication formula; this lane derived it from the five-term relation, and proved the whole chain sorry-free in Lean, which the literature does not do.
verdict.extend_is_zagier: FiveTwoRogersExtend.extend is Zagier's definition verbatim. Route 13's repair was the standard one -- now checked against the source, not memory.
verdict.deriv_is_zagier: hasDerivAt_rogersL is Zagier's L'(x), verbatim, and he names that formula as the route to all the functional equations -- which is how Abel was proved here.
verdict.CORRECTION: qou-rstq claimed the purely-imaginary cut jump 'is written down nowhere'. It is in Zagier Ch. I SS3: Li_2 jumps by 2*pi*i*log|z| across [1, inf). Standard; cite it rather than claiming folklore.
